Bayesian PCA Imputation on a Flanking Window per Column

Source: R/mi_pca_flank.R
mipca_flank.Rd

Impute each target column from the columns near it by location, such as the CpGs within some distance of a CpG. mipca_flank_plan() finds each target's window, and mipca_flank() fits mipca() on each window and keeps the target's draws.

Usage

mipca_flank_plan(
  obj,
  location,
  window_size,
  subset,
  min_window_n,
  colmax = 0.95,
  abb = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'si_flank_plan'
print(x, n = 10L, ...)

mipca_flank_window(plan, subset)

mipca_flank(
  plan,
  rank,
  seed,
  transform,
  prop_diag = 0.5,
  iter_sampling = 100,
  iter_warmup = 100,
  thin = 1,
  nu = Inf,
  chains = 4L,
  spectra = spectra_opts(),
  init = 1,
  .progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix with samples in rows and features in columns. Row and column names are required and must be unique. NA and NaN values are imputed.

location

Numeric. The position of each column of obj, such as a genomic coordinate, sorted in ascending order.

window_size

Numeric. Distance from the target, in the units of location, that its window covers on each side.

subset

Character or integer vector. In mipca_flank_plan(), the target columns. In mipca_flank_window(), one target of the plan. By name or by number.

min_window_n

Integer. Minimum number of columns in a window, the target included, at least 2. mipca_flank() needs at least rank + 2.

colmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Columns missing a larger proportion of their values are left out of every window, and are not imputed. Defaults to 0.95.

abb

Optional character or integer vector. Columns to draw by approximate Bayesian bootstrap instead of by the model. They are left out of every window. abb_cols() proposes them. Defaults to NULL.

x

A si_flank_plan object.

n

Integer. Number of rows of the table to print. Defaults to 10.

...

Not used.

plan

A si_flank_plan object. The plan mipca_flank_plan() returns.

rank

Integer. Number of principal components in the model. Use mipca_tune() to choose the rank on held-out values.

seed

Integer. Seed for the sampler.

transform

Character or a transform object. The scale the model is fitted on: "identity", "logit_biwhiten", or an object from tf_identity(), tf_sv() or tf_biwhiten(). See Details in mipca().

prop_diag

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Proportion of each column's missing values on which summary() computes Rhat and ESS. 0 is refused. Defaults to 0.5.

iter_sampling

Integer. Number of draws kept per chain. Defaults to 100.

iter_warmup

Integer. Number of iterations discarded at the start of each chain, 0 or more. Defaults to 100.

thin

Integer. After warmup, each chain keeps one iteration in every thin, so it runs iter_sampling * thin iterations to keep iter_sampling draws. Defaults to 1.

nu

Numeric. Degrees of freedom of the noise drawn for a missing value: Inf for Gaussian noise, or a number above 2 for Student-t noise of the same variance. Defaults to Inf. Can be chosen by mipca_tune().

chains

Integer. Number of independent chains. Defaults to 4.

spectra

A spectra_opts object. Settings for the eigensolver, from spectra_opts().

init

Numeric. How widely each chain's starting values are spread: each missing value starts at a random draw whose standard deviation is init times its column's observed standard deviation. Must be positive. Defaults to 1.

.progress

Logical. If TRUE, report progress through the windows. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

  • mipca_flank_plan(): a si_flank_plan object, holding obj, the settings and the table targets.

  • mipca_flank(): a finalized fit of class si_mi over the targets, as mipca() returns.

  • mipca_flank_window(): a numeric matrix, the columns of the target's window.

  • print(): x, invisibly.

Details

The window. A target's window is the columns within window_size of it on location, on both sides. Columns that are constant, have fewer than two observed values, miss more than colmax of their values, or are listed in abb are left out.

The columns read. mipca_flank_plan() reads a column only if a window can hold it, or if it is a target listed in abb, and refuses an Inf in any column it reads. It does not read the other columns, so an Inf in one of them is not refused. mipca_flank() reads only the targets listed in abb and the columns of the windows it fits.

The plan. plan$targets has one row per target, in column order: its column number target and name, its number of missing values n_miss, the first and last column of its window start and end, the number of columns in the window window_n, and its status:

  • "impute": fitted on its window.

  • "clean": no missing values.

  • "abb": listed in abb, and drawn from its own observed values.

  • "inadmissible": constant, with fewer than two observed values, or missing more than colmax. Its missing values stay NA.

  • "window_small": fewer than min_window_n columns in its window. Its missing values stay NA.

A plan in which no target with missing values can be imputed is refused. print() shows the count per status and the first n rows.

The rank and nu. Choose them on one target's window: pass mipca_flank_window(plan, target) to mipca_tune(), then give the rank and nu to mipca_flank(). The default n_cols of mipca_tune() holds out values in at least 50 columns, more than a window may have, so pass a smaller n_cols there.

The fit. The result holds the targets in the order of plan$targets. Its completed matrices hold NA where a target was not imputed, and print() counts those columns. A target's draws depend on seed and its column number in obj only, so dropping another target from the plan leaves them unchanged.

Failures. A window whose fit fails stops the run, with the target's name in the message.

See also

  • mipca() to fit the whole matrix at once.

  • mipca_tune() to choose the rank on a window.

  • cbind() to join the fits of several matrices, such as one per chromosome.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sim <- sim_mat(n = 50, p = 200, beta = TRUE)
obj <- sim$input
location <- seq_len(ncol(obj))

# Windows of 20 columns on each side of three targets
plan <- mipca_flank_plan(
  obj,
  location,
  window_size = 20,
  subset = c(49, 102, 150),
  min_window_n = 10
)
plan
#> si_flank_plan: 3 targets on a 50 x 200 matrix, nothing fitted
#>   status: impute 3
#>  target       name n_miss start end window_n status
#>      49  feature49     10    29  69       41 impute
#>     102 feature102     10    82 122       41 impute
#>     150 feature150     10   130 170       41 impute
#>   next: mipca_flank(x, rank, seed, transform) imputes.
#>         mipca_flank_window(x, subset) gives one target's window to tune on.

# One target's window, to choose the rank on
win <- mipca_flank_window(plan, 150)
dim(win)
#> [1] 50 41

fit <- mipca_flank(plan, rank = 2, seed = 1, transform = "logit_biwhiten")
#> processing window 1 of 3
#> processing window 2 of 3
#> processing window 3 of 3
fit
#> si_mi fit: 50 x 3, 30 imputed cells, 400 draws
#>   next: as.matrix() with 'draw' for a completed matrix, summary() for Rhat and ESS
